Edgemont Village is a neighbourhood in the District of North Vancouver and one of the District's six Village Centres (with Lions Gate, Queensdale, Maplewood, Parkgate and Deep Cove) in its Upper Capilano area; its core is the Edgemont Boulevard shopping strip at Highland Boulevard, where the Capilano Library (3045 Highland Boulevard) sits — described by the library as "located in the heart of Edgemont Village." Nearby areas: Canyon Heights (west), Capilano Highlands (north), Delbrook and Upper Lonsdale (east), Queensdale (southeast).

This guide covers Edgemont's condo buildings, townhome complexes and land: what each source verifies, the local rules, and what buyers ask. Seniors housing has its own page.
Condo buildings in Edgemont
Edgemont (Edgemont Village) is in the District of North Vancouver — not the City of North Vancouver. Its governing bylaws are OCP Bylaw 7900 and Zoning Bylaw 3210.
Connaught (Grosvenor Edgemont), 3230 Connaught Crescent (unit listings use 3220 Connaught Crescent for the same project)

A concrete mixed-use project by Grosvenor over ground-floor shops anchored by Thrifty Foods and Shoppers Drug Mart, with 82 homes: 59 condos and 23 townhomes. Built 2016–2019, so homes here are resales, not presales. A current listing shows a 2019 condo with cats allowed, a bike room and an exercise centre.
Edgemont Villa — 3151 Connaught Crescent (Edgemont Village)

The village's age-restricted strata: freehold strata, built 2003, with only 20 condos. Listings describe a "boutique 55+ residence" in the heart of Edgemont Village, with underground parking (one stall), an elevator and storage, and fees covering electricity, garbage, grounds, hot water and water. Confirm the 55+ bylaw wording in the Form B and bylaws before relying on it.
Crescentview at Edgemont — 3121 Connaught Crescent

A three-storey wood-frame building of 22 condos by VPAC Construction Group, designed by RLA Architects, completed in 2023 at the edge of the village shops. The developer says short-term rentals like Airbnb aren't allowed; confirm the bylaw on the Form B.

items.t: All the condos are around the village core, on one short crescent: Edgemont Villa (3151), Crescentview (3121) and Connaught (3220/3230) on Connaught Crescent, a few blocks from the Edgemont Boulevard shops. The rest of the plateau between Mackay Creek and Mosquito Creek is mostly freehold detached houses.
Catchments for any other Edgemont address — including the Connaught Crescent buildings.

The village's main grocery site, at the Edgemont and Ridgewood gateway, was redeveloped by Grosvenor as a low-rise mixed-use project with a bigger grocery store, ground-floor shops and 82 condos and townhomes.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Edgemont

items.t: Plans and zoning (District of North Vancouver, not the City): the Official Community Plan (Bylaw 7900) directs growth to town and village centres, with Edgemont as one of six village centres and the surrounding streets staying low-density. Since June 2024, all single-family lots inside the urban boundary can have a house, a secondary suite and a coach house; since December 2023, a suite can be up to 49% of the house with no minimum size, and coach houses can be two storeys. The District's GEOweb map shows eligible lots allowing up to 3 units at 280 m² or less, 4 on larger lots, and 6 on larger lots within 400 m of a frequent bus stop; provincial law (Bill 25) requires full small-scale housing density by June 30, 2026, and the District's changes were still being prepared in spring 2026. The plan has development permit areas for natural environment, streamside, wildfire, creek and slope hazards; Mackay Creek and Mosquito Creek run through the neighbourhood's ravines.

District of North Vancouver property taxes: 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 1, 2026; the 2026 residential municipal rate is 1.83419 and the total residential rate is 3.28195 per $1,000 of assessed value, and single-family utility fees include water at $932.80 and sewer/drainage at $1,255.60 (combined single-family utilities $2,571 in 2026). Strata units carry their own utility arrangements — confirm on the Form B.

blocks.text: Good to know about Edgemont condos

items.t: Edgemont's entire condo supply stands on one crescent. All three buildings — Edgemont Villa (2003), Connaught (2019) and Crescentview (2023) — are on Connaught Crescent, a short walk apart beside the library, grocery and cafés. A "condos in Edgemont" search that returns anything on another street deserves a second look before a drive.

Connaught answers to two civic numbers and two project totals. Current unit listings use 3220 Connaught Crescent while the developer/presale sources use 3230 Connaught Crescent for the same project, and the totals run 82 homes (Grosvenor: 59 apartments + 23 townhomes) against 83 apartments and townhomes in an NVRC document. Settle the address and the unit's strata plan from the title and Form B, not from either marketing figure.

The village grocery site was rebuilt around the condos. The Grosvenor Edgemont project redeveloped the village's main grocery site at the Edgemont/Ridgewood gateway with an expanded grocery store (Thrifty Foods), ground-floor shops and its 82 condos and townhomes — the retail that Edgemont Villa, Crescentview and Amica residents walk to is this renewed core, not the strip it replaced.

items.t: Nearby areas: Canyon Heights (west), Capilano Highlands (north), Delbrook and Upper Lonsdale (east), Queensdale (southeast). The MLS sub-area name as the board (Greater Vancouver REALTORS®) uses it is Edgemont.

Where the townhouses are: in and right around the village, in two places. One is Connaught Crescent (the Connaught project's 23 townhouses, beside its 59 apartments) and the other is Edgemont Boulevard on the east side of the village (Edgemont Ridge Estates, 2425 Edgemont Boulevard).

Recreation and hazards: Murdo Frazer Park is the District park in the Edgemont area (6 tennis courts and 6 pickleball courts in the District's Outdoor Sports Courts Optimization Strategy, approved July 21, 2025), and the Delbrook Community Recreation Centre, 851 West Queens Road, is the nearest full-service recreation centre. Grouse Mountain (6400 Nancy Greene Way) and Capilano Suspension Bridge Park (3735 Capilano Road) are in neighbouring Upper Capilano. The District designates Natural Hazard Development Permit Areas for slope and creek hazards; Mackay Creek and Mosquito Creek run through the neighbourhood's ravines.

These rebuilt shops are what residents of Edgemont Villa, Crescentview, Connaught and Amica walk to.

Land shape: predominantly single-detached homes on sloped, view-capable lots on the plateau between the Mackay Creek and Mosquito Creek ravines; attached housing concentrates in and immediately around the village core. District growth is directed to its town and village centres under the OCP, while surrounding established streets remain low-density.

Schools (SD44 North Vancouver): Highlands Elementary (K–7, 3150 Colwood Drive) and Canyon Heights Elementary (K–7, 4501 Highland Boulevard) split the neighbourhood, feeding Handsworth Secondary (Grades 8–12, 1033 Handsworth Road). Catchments for other Edgemont addresses remain address-specific.

Recreation anchors: Murdo Frazer Park is the Edgemont-area District park (6 tennis courts and 6 pickleball courts in the District's Outdoor Sports Courts Optimization Strategy, approved July 21, 2025); the Delbrook Community Recreation Centre (851 West Queens Road) is the nearest NVRC full-service centre; Grouse Mountain (6400 Nancy Greene Way) and Capilano Suspension Bridge Park (3735 Capilano Road) sit in neighbouring Upper Capilano.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Edgemont

items.t: OCP — District of North Vancouver Official Community Plan Bylaw 7900, under which Edgemont is designated one of the District's six village centres and growth is directed to town and village centres.
Zoning — District of North Vancouver Zoning Bylaw 3210: — District numbers only; City of North Vancouver bylaws belong to the City and are never imported here.

Small-scale housing: the District's GEOweb map shows eligible lots allowing up to 3 units at 280 m² or less, 4 on larger lots, and 6 on larger lots within 400 m of a frequent bus stop. Provincial law (Bill 25, November 2025) requires full small-scale housing density by June 30, 2026; the District's changes were still being prepared in spring 2026, as part of a zoning rewrite running into late 2027. Check GEOweb for a specific lot.

Hazard permit areas: Schedule B of the District OCP establishes Development Permit Areas for Protection of the Natural Environment, Streamside Protection, Wildfire Hazard, Creek Hazard and Slope Hazard, and the District's GEOweb flood construction level data is defined as modelled flood water levels for a 2100 (2080s) horizon plus 0.6 m. Creek-adjacent and steep lots warrant a GeoWeb check before pricing a renovation or rebuild — slope and creek DPAs can add geotechnical and permit cost.

items.t: No District park is named "Edgemont Park" (Nov 1, 2026). Murdo Frazer Park is the Edgemont-area District park, described in a District planning table as "predominantly natural area and trails with some community uses (pitch and putt and tennis courts)." A listing that refers to "Edgemont Park" is not naming a District park.

The flood construction level here is a 2100-horizon model (Nov 1, 2026). The District's GEOweb flood construction level data is defined as modelled flood water levels for a 2100 (2080s) horizon plus 0.6 m — a future-climate figure, not a historical flood line, which changes how a creek-lot buyer should read it.
The village's main grocery site is the redevelopment (Nov 1, 2026).

The library is the civic anchor, in the village's heart (Nov 1, 2026). The Capilano Library at 3045 Highland Boulevard is described by the North Vancouver District Public Library as "located in the heart of Edgemont Village" and "a cornerstone of its community," with a quiet study room, storytimes and technology training — walkable-village claims hold only within a few blocks of this strip.
The creek greenways are designated as critical environmental areas in the Official Community Plan.

items.t: The usual home: Edgemont is mostly single detached homes on sloped lots, many with views, on the plateau between the Mackay Creek and Mosquito Creek ravines. The District's Official Community Plan describes its existing residential neighbourhoods as largely detached houses, and attached housing here is in and right around the village.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect duplexes in Edgemont

items.t: District of North Vancouver plans and zoning: the Official Community Plan is Bylaw 7900. It directs growth to the District's town and village centres, and names Edgemont as one of six village centres while the surrounding established streets stay low-density. Hazards: the plan sets Development Permit Areas for Protection of the Natural Environment, Streamside Protection, Wildfire Hazard, Creek Hazard and Slope Hazard, and the District provides property-level hazard reports through GeoWeb. Check Edgemont's creek ravines and sloped lots before you build or buy.

The District's GEOweb SSMUH classification shows non-exempt lots potentially allowing up to 3 units at 280 m² or less, up to 4 units above 280 m², and up to 6 units above 280 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit bus stop. The Province's Bill 25 (November 2025) requires full SSMUH density by June 30, 2026; the District's compliance amendments were still in preparation in spring 2026, tied to the Zoning Bylaw Rewrite project, whose timeline extends into Q3 2027. A duplex (two units) sits inside even the lowest of those tiers where the lot is non-exempt — but the specific lot's classification is read off GEOweb, not assumed.

faq.q: How many condo buildings does Edgemont Village actually have?
faq.a: Everything else in Edgemont is detached houses, plus the Amica care residence, which is rental.

faq.q: Is Connaught a presale I need to worry about completing?
faq.a: No. Grosvenor says construction started in 2016 and finished in 2019. The homes are resales, so you review the strata documents and the building's condition; there's no assignment or completion risk.

faq.q: My spouse is under 55. Can we both live in Edgemont Villa?
faq.a: Under provincial strata rules, a younger spouse or partner of a resident who meets the age requirement (or holds a legacy exemption) is exempt. Live-in caregivers are also exempt, as are children under 19 in the resident's care and adult children the resident cared for before 19 — Regulation 7.01, expanded effective May 1, 2023.

faq.q: Can I rent out an Edgemont condo?
faq.a: Long-term rentals: yes; rental bans have been void across BC since November 24, 2022, though in a 55+ building the tenant still has to meet the age bylaw or an exemption. Short-term rentals: a strata can still ban or limit them, and Crescentview says Airbnb-type rentals aren't allowed; confirm the bylaw on the Form B.

faq.q: How many townhouse complexes does Edgemont actually have?
faq.a: Everything else attached in the village is apartment condos on Connaught Crescent or the Amica care residence, which is rental.

faq.q: Is Edgemont Villa a townhouse complex? It keeps appearing in my townhouse search.
faq.a: It is the village's known 55+ building (listing-stated; confirm the exact bylaw on the Form B) — a 55+ apartment, not a townhouse.

faq.q: Is Connaught a presale I need to worry about completing?
faq.a: No. Grosvenor says construction started in 2016 and finished in 2019. The homes (59 apartments and 23 townhouses) are resales, so you review the strata documents and the building's condition; there's no assignment or completion risk.

faq.q: Can I buy just one side of a duplex in Edgemont?
faq.a: Only if that side is legally separate — a strata lot in a strata plan, or its own fee-simple lot from a subdivision. Check the title first.

faq.q: Is the unit at 3669 Edgemont Boulevard a half duplex I can buy on its own title?
faq.a: A single listing calls it a duplex-style townhouse unit built in 1971 within a common property of 8 owners; no source verifies a complex name, strata title or unit tenure to the counting standard.

faq.q: Can I add units to an Edgemont house instead of hunting for a duplex?
faq.a: In many cases yes as a housing form: Since June 2024 the District permits a principal dwelling plus a secondary suite (up to 49% of the house) plus a coach house — three units total — on single-family zoned lots within the Urban Containment Boundary, subject to the lot's zone and any creek/slope development permit areas. A suite or coach house is not a separable title, though — those units cannot be sold separately without strata or subdivision.

faq.q: What hazard checks are specific to Edgemont?
faq.a: Slope and creek hazards — the District maps Natural Hazard Development Permit Areas (including Creek Hazard and Slope Hazard) and offers property-level GeoWeb reports; ravine and steep lots should be checked before purchase or design work.
